defs_parts: Six labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Video only: the term comes from a video lecture, and is not in the course text or on the term list.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: MCP drives a live Blender, and a bpy script runs it headless.
Add the python exit code flag, or a broken script exits zero.
Blender is Z-up, and the plus Y Up option puts its Z on Godot's Y.
Apply transforms, so the scale lives in the mesh and not on the node.
A name suffix builds collision only when the import setting is on.
A name is a claim, and only a number read from the file is evidence.
bookends.segment: Name The Term, Measure The Prop
bookends.command: Quiz me on moving a model from Blender into Godot, with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms unit scale, up axis, apply transforms, node scale, GLB, name suffix, collision shape, convex, triangle count and claim versus measurement. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case is a game-making situation, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and said why its look-alike does not fit.
